title: Application
for: Projects that build and ship software: apps, sites, tools, games, services. Adds specs with acceptance criteria, the triple-check QA, gates that must pass before commit, releases, performance, data safety and security.
notFor: Knowledge or context projects that don't build software: it would add machinery the project never uses.

codeRules.message: untrusted HTML through innerHTML; sanitize it or build DOM nodes (docs/checks/app-standards.md)
native alert/confirm/prompt; use the app's own dialog
execFile on a .cmd/.bat without a shell is unsafe; use spawn with shell:true and fixed arguments
eval on dynamic input; parse the data instead

menu: | A0 | Set the foundation | app-foundation.md | set the app's foundation with me: security baseline, performance budgets with numbers, usability defaults and gates, then build the scaffolding that enforces them |
| A1 | Build a feature | feature.md | build this feature: spec with acceptance criteria, plan, build, triple-check QA, independent review until SHIP, release notes |
| A2 | Fix a bug | bugfix.md | fix this bug: reproduce it, write a failing test, fix the cause, prove it passes, look for siblings |
| A3 | QA | qa.md | QA failed on this: find what slipped and why, fix it, re-run the full triple check, and harden the process so it can't slip again |
| A4 | Release | release.md | prepare a release: gates pass, release notes, version, attribution and secrets scan; ask me before pushing or publishing |
| A5 | Performance | perf.md | make this faster: measure before, find the real cost, change one thing, measure after with the same tool |
| A6 | Change stored data | data-change.md | change how this data is stored without any loss: backup, migrate on copies, test the restore |
| A7 | Security review | security-review.md | review the app's security baseline item by item with evidence, and fix what fails |
| A8 | Install / update | install-update.md | change or verify installing, launching or updating, with a test matrix for me to run |
flags: | --no-commit | make and verify the change but don't commit |
| --sweep | run the change through a QA sweep (independent auditors, rounds until nothing new) |
precedence: Something is broken → `bugfix.md`; something new or different → `feature.md`; only speed → `perf.md`; only the look → `gui.md` (gui pack).
The user says "QA" about work that was delivered → `qa.md` §1 first (QA failed), then the original runbook.
layout: Security baseline, performance budgets, usability defaults, quality gates
Set with the user before feature work; features are verified against it
One spec per feature: the request, acceptance criteria, plan, verification log
Each criterion is PASS in the answer
Release notes as acceptance scripts: what changed, try it fast, try it for real
One line per escaped bug or rejected result → the check it created
Read before risky or taste-driven work
Independent review reports (PASS/FAIL table, SHIP or FIX)

requirements.message: Fill docs/foundation.md with the user (no <...> left, status: set) and list the security tests, budget script and gates you built, each with its result.

require.answerMatches: ^#{1,6}\s*verification\b(?=[\s\S]*\bautomated\b)(?=[\s\S]*(real app|manual|ran the app|in the app))(?=[\s\S]*\breview\b)(?=[\s\S]*(budget|foundation))(?=[\s\S]*(still weak|not verified|known issues|nothing weak))

requirements.message: Code changed: add a Verification section with Automated (commands and results), Real app (what was exercised, screenshot paths), Budgets (still within docs/foundation.md, with numbers when performance-relevant), Independent review (SHIP/FIX and the report path) and Still weak (docs/checks/qa-standards.md).
A feature needs an independent review that ends in SHIP (fix and re-review until it does). Quote the verdict and the report path.
Write or update docs/specs/<feature>.md with numbered acceptance criteria and the plan, and mark each criterion PASS in the answer.
Write release notes in docs/releases/ (what changed, try it fast, try it for real).
A release needs its notes in docs/releases/ and a clean attribution scan (node tools/hooks/git-guard.mjs scan) quoted in the answer.
A bugfix needs a regression test that failed before the fix and passes after it.
The user said QA, so QA failed: report What slipped, Why QA missed it, Fix, and Process change, and add a line to docs/lessons.md.
QA runbook: report what was found. An incident gets "What slipped" and the rest of the incident report; a sweep lists its rounds, findings with evidence, fixes and what is left.
Performance work needs before and after numbers from the same tool in the answer.
Name the backup, the restore test, and the record counts before and after.
Give a table of every security item with PASS/FAIL/N/A and the evidence.
Write the install/update test matrix into the release notes, each case marked tested or for the user to run.
Behaviour changed: raise the version number (the last part for fixes, the middle part for new features). Turned on by: node tools/packs.mjs configure app --version-file <file>.
Add a dated line to docs/CHANGELOG.md.
Bugfix: state the root cause in the answer ("Root cause: <what and why>"), found before the fix (debug skill), not a description of the symptom.
